summary: Chiew Hui Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (2004–2013) and served as Discipline Chair at the University of Sydney in 2013.

Chih-fu Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He served at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies as Director (attested 2003–2007) and Honorary Director (retired December 26, 2006; attested 2026).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, also studying under Nobuyoshi Yamabe and Canshan Cheng, and held faculty posts at Fo Guang University (attested 2016, 2026).

Chihiro Nakayashiki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, educated at Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific, Kyoto, and Himachal Pradesh universities. Academic appointments include JSPS fellow posts (2014–2016, 2019–2022) and visiting researcher at the University of Edinburgh (2019–2020).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar educated at Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku University (1943–1947), and Yamaguchi University (1950–1952).
Chijun Hamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute in 1978.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a master's degree at the University of British Columbia under Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Aklujkar, and earned a PhD from the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura.
Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued traditional studies under Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980).
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied traditionally under Khenpo Gangshar (~1957–1959) and held a post at the British Library.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy who studied under Thomé H. Fang, Bingnan Li, and Lobsang Palden Tenpe Dronme. He taught at Chinese Culture University and headed the Pure Land Learning College Association.

Ching Keng is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. He held faculty posts at National Chengchi University (~2012–2020) and National Taiwan University (2021).

Ching-mei Shyu works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University (2008) supervised by Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indologist. He served as Professor at Presidency University, held a post at Bethune College (attested 1941), and was Publication Secretary of the Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat (attested 1960).

Chintaman Ganesh Kashikar (1910–2007) was an Indology scholar who served as Assistant Secretary at Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1941) and as Professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, served as a Director there in 1996, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He held leadership positions at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Sōji-ji (~1957–1967), and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968) and held teaching appointments at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and Tokoha University (attested 1989).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1907–1911) and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa. He became a professor at Otani University (1919) and co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society (1921).

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Vienna (PhD 1990–1994), later serving as professor at the University of Tsukuba.
